reason: One successful rating required 9.7 minutes. Use up to four isolated workers to finish the existing 56-rating scope, with a new one-rating scheduler canary before fan-out.
pilot_scope: One already planned rubric10 repeat rating, launched by the identical foreground Python controller, shell environment and four-worker scheduling mode used by the fill, with a queue containing only this job.
unchanged: Frozen evaluator adapter, runner, 56 complete prompts, inputs, both instruments, schemas, output paths, Opus 5 selector and high effort, explicit CBORG route and $5 per-attempt limit.
failure_policy: Stop new launches on observed failure, retain and drain every active evaluator, no automatic retry of any existing attempt.
limits: One-job canary verifies worker credential inheritance and persisted output; concurrent service rate limits, cross-item contention and long-tail inputs are unmeasured until fill.

supersedes_registration.reason: #1342: prepare arguments before the stop check; serialize signal observation with dequeue/spawn using a short signal-mask critical section; workers unblock inherited stop signals before preflight. No scheduler model calls have occurred.

interrupt_policy: SIGINT and SIGTERM request a controller stop without propagating to worker sessions; active workers retain their original runner timeout and finish with evidence. A forced SIGKILL or host loss remains outside graceful-drain guarantees.
launch_boundary: A stop observed during preparation leaves the job queued. Signal delivery is deferred only through the short atomic launch decision, then observed by the controller; existing workers remain in separate sessions.
